decisions.reason: The source says operators preferred a visible warning when the source file arrived late; the summary and TEAM attribution preserve that preference without claiming implementation.
The source establishes only that operators preferred a warning. It does not say the warning was implemented or attribute implementation to the person.
The source says the person planned a rollout for next month and explicitly says it was not completed; the summary accurately preserves both points.
The source explicitly says the planned rollout has not been completed.
The source says “we discussed” the database migration and did not perform it; the team-level summary accurately reflects that.
The source says the migration was discussed but not performed, contradicting the claim that the person performed it.
The source says the team deployed Beacon and that the person's only contribution was writing the user guide; it also says the person did not build the model or deployment.
The source attributes the model integration to the person's brother and explicitly says the person did not build the model or deployment.

The source supports one-time Docker exposure in a guided local exercise and explicitly states there was no production deployment experience; the summary and EXPOSURE attribution retain those qualifications.
The source describes only a one-time guided local exercise and explicitly denies production deployment experience; it does not support proficiency.
The source says the person trained twelve coworkers in two workshops; the personal attribution is accurate.
The source says the person trained coworkers but had not managed employees, so it does not support managing twelve direct reports.
